content: If you are interested in taking over this page and applying to become the Editor-in-Chief for this topic, please note that there can be one or more Editors-in-Chief. Additionally, you may apply to serve as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for one of the subtopics listed below. To express your interest in either role, please send us an email. Be sure to include your curriculum vitae (CV) and/or a biographical sketch as part of your application. Overview Pronunciation refers to the way in which a word or a language is typically spoken. It also encompasses the manner in which an individual articulates a word. The pronunciation of a word can vary significantly among different individuals or groups due to a variety of factors, including: The region where they were raised. The region where they currently reside. The presence of any speech disorders or defects. Their ethnic background. Their social class. Their level of education. Linguistic Terminology In linguistics, individuals are analyzed based on the units of sound, known as phones, that they use in their language. The field of linguistics that studies these sound units is called phonetics. Phones that serve the same functional role in a language are grouped into categories known as phonemes. The study of phonemes is referred to as phonemics, phonematics, or phonology.
